INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

A meeting of the Inglewood Arts Commission was convened on March 16, 2022, via Zoom. Commissioner Metcalf
called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Roll Call

Present
  Commissioner Jacques Lesure, Commissioner at Large
  Commissioner Althea Metcalf, District One
  Commissioner Phyllis Battle, District Three
  Commissioner Vicki Perryman-Banks, District Four
  Sabrina Barnes, Director - Parks, Recreation, and Community Services
  Helen Lessick, Public Art Consultant
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
Absent
  Commissioner Onna Ehrlich-Bell, District Two

Public Comments

  None

Approval of the Minutes

  Commissioner Lesure made a motion to approve the minutes from January 19, 2022. Commissioner Battle
seconded and the minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Battle, Metcalf, Lesure, and Banks
  Nays: None

Special Presentation

  Camille Delaney-McNeil, Director of Beckman YOLA Center, Los Angeles Philharmonic Association with
CARS-LA introduced herself and Lucas Rivera. Mr. Rivera is charged with putting together a family friendly festival
celebrating the Best of Inglewood that will include numerous artist workshops and stage performances. Helen Lessick
asked Mr. Rivera for the date. Albert Montanez stated the festival will be held on May 14 and 15, 2022 with a
tentative time of 11:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. We anticipate about 5,000 people each day. Ms. Delaney-McNeil stated this
is an opportunity to focus on arts and culture, not settling with the traditional vendor setup or the occasional
performances but incorporating interactive art workshops that people can walk up, to participate in, and take
something back with them making this a unique event. Commissioner Metcalf asked what she meant by interactive.
Ms. Delaney-McNeil stated for example, we are taking artist Malika Beckford and her poetry and aligning her with a
live doodle artist. They will hold a live spoken word workshop that incorporates live doodling. A large community
canvas will be available where the public can respond to the spoken word and create their own art. Director Barnes
stated the ideas sound awesome and looks forward to seeing the concentration of artists, the energy, and the
opportunity to network with the community all in one place. Commissioner Metcalf asked how is the event being
  1
   INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

advertised. Mr. Rivera stated there will be different forms of advertisement including the Getty's marketing, the Artists
and their networks, and CARS-LA will create several social media marketing campaigns. Ms. Delaney-McNeil added
there will also be an outreach to the stakeholders, YOLA families and a list of other networks. Director Barnes asked
for information on how to be a part of the event to share with the public.

Staff Report

  Staff presented a staff report recommending the Arts Commission recommend the City Manager approve a
professional services contract with Art Care Conservation for $35,300 to first clean and conserve the mural Parks
Make Life Better by Wayne Healy, Michelle Glass, and others, at Darby Park; and then clean and conserve the mural
Pathways to Success by Adwin David Brown, Chris Mercier, and youth, at Rogers Park. Helen Lessick gave a verbal
report and background information regarding fine art conservation.

  Commissioner Lesure made a motion to approve the staff report and Commissioner Battle seconded. The
motion was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Battle, Banks, Lesure, and Metcalf
  Nays: None

  Staff presented a staff report recommending the Arts Commission recommend the City Manager approve a
professional services contract with art conservators Sculpture Conservation Studios in the amount of $11,970, to
clean and repair the public artwork History of Transportation and the associated signage. Helen Lessick gave a
verbal and visual report about History of Transportation, the largest public artwork located at Grevillea Art Park.

  Commissioner Lesure made a motion to approve the staff report and Commissioner Banks seconded. The
motion was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Battle, Banks, Lesure, and Metcalf
  Nays: None

Verbal Reports

  Helen Lessick gave a verbal report with updates regarding the following:
    Art and Culture Walking Tour Series is an educational and informational walking tour intended to introduce
  Inglewood residents, visitors, and businesses to the cultural heritage of the City of Inglewood. The tour series
  consists of six (6) planned tours online and in print format. Each tour is a one-hour walking tour exploring
  public art, architecture, and cultural sites. Two (2) additional series have been added and include the
  Downtown Market Street area and the Crenshaw Corridor. The new additions can be found on the public art
  web page at www.Inglewoodpublicart.org/Explore. Tours to be completed are the Sports and Entertainment
  District, Gardens and Green Spaces, and West Beach Avenue. Commissioner Metcalf asked for clarity on
  what a walking tour is. Ms. Lessick stated it is a self-guided tour that shows points of interest within the

  2
   INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

  community focusing on arts and culture. Director Barnes added a map that will guide you on a path to
  observe the various artwork is also available for print online.
    Rogers Park Artist in Residence (RPAIR) Project and exhibition update - the exhibition is currently up at the
  Inglewood Public Library located in the lobby area. The It Takes a Village quilt is complete and on display
  through April 2, 2022 during regular business hours. On Saturday, February 26, 2022, an event was held to
  meet and acknowledge the artists.

Public Comments

  None

Commissioner’s Comments

  Helen Lessick shared information about Inglewood Artist, Ulysses Jenkins who occupied a studio in
Inglewood for about 25 years. He has a show from February 6, 2022 through May 15, 2022 at the Hammer Museum
located at UCLA. The event is free and a Q & A will be held tomorrow March 17, 2022. Mr. Jenkins will be in
attendance.

  Commissioner Battle stated everything she heard discussed tonight is exciting and is very happy to see all
the wonderful things that are going on Inglewood. Commissioner Banks echoed Commissioner Battle’s sentiments.

With no further business, the meeting was adjourned at 7:29 p.m.
